h1: Tata Elxsi: an infotainment system and instrument cluster designed for the glance
subtitle: We designed two in-car HMI systems for Tata Elxsi, an infotainment interface and a digital instrument cluster for connected vehicles, working within a tier-one supplier's engineering constraints.

cta.heading: Designing for the road?
cta.body: Tell us about the hardware and the programme. We'll tell you how we'd model the glance budget.

sections.heading: Executive summary
sections.answer: In a car, every glance at the screen is attention taken from the road. Designit designed two HMI systems for Tata Elxsi, an infotainment interface and a digital instrument cluster, around glance duration and context, keeping essential controls reachable and simplifying the interface as driving demands more attention.
body: What changed is how the interface behaves: a layered interaction model instead of everything at once, an adaptive UI that simplifies at speed, a cluster that uses the digital medium for context rather than imitating analogue gauges, and interactions validated in driving-simulator conditions.

sections.heading: Project facts
items: In-vehicle infotainment system and digital instrument cluster
Drivers, from tech-savvy to those who only want music and navigation

sections.heading: The business and driver problem
paras: Existing infotainment systems were either too simple, missing features drivers expect from their phones, or too complex, creating dangerous distraction. Early digital clusters simply mimicked analogue gauges and wasted what a digital display can do. Both systems had to meet safety guidelines while serving very different drivers.

items.title: Safety standards and information needs
items.body: Guidelines on driver distraction and research into what drivers need to see in each context.

items.title: A layered interaction model
items.body: Essential controls always accessible; depth available without demanding attention.

items.title: Adaptive display modes
items.body: Information prioritised by driving context, with transitions that preserve focus.

items.title: Simulator testing
items.body: Interactions tested in driving-simulator conditions, because desk evaluation underestimates glance cost.

items.title: Automotive design system
items.body: Readability under all lighting conditions, with dark-mode-first design to reduce night glare.

sections.heading: Key lessons
items: Layer the interface. Keep essentials one glance away; let depth wait.
Simplify as speed rises. The interface should demand less when driving demands more.
Use the digital medium. Context beats imitating analogue gauges.
Design night mode first. Glare is a safety issue, not a theme.

items.title: Infotainment System
items.desc: Next-gen in-vehicle infotainment balancing safety with intuitive controls.

items.title: Digital Instrument Cluster
items.desc: Digital cockpit instrument cluster with clear visual hierarchy and adaptive display.

faq.q: What did Designit design for Tata Elxsi?
faq.a: Two in-car HMI systems: an infotainment interface and a digital instrument cluster for connected vehicles, designed within a tier-one supplier's engineering constraints. The work was also published on Behance.
Interactions were tested in driving-simulator conditions, because evaluating automotive interfaces at a desk underestimates how much attention they cost.
